It was generated by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium, a Precision Public Health grand challenge project funded by the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program, whose stated goal is a flagship, standardized, and ethically sourced dataset of 10,000 voices linked to health information to fuel research and discovery in voice biomarkers. The dataset couples acoustic recordings of voice, speech, breathing and cough tasks with detailed participant metadata: clinical diagnoses (voice, neurological, mood, respiratory and pediatric voice/speech disorders), validated questionnaires, and demographics. Public releases contain derived representations of the audio (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, articulatory and phonetic features, pitch and loudness measures) rather than the original waveforms; access to raw audio is restricted to a separate controlled-access mechanism. Data are collected at multiple sites across North America. value: "The Bridge2AI-Voice (B2AI-Voice) dataset is a large, ethically sourced, and demographically diverse voice dataset linked to health information, released by the NIH's Bridge2AI initiative. It is produced by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium, a Precision Public Health grand challenge project funded by the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program, whose stated goal is to create a flagship, standardized, ethically sourced dataset of voices linked to health information to fuel research and discovery in voice biomarkers. Data are collected prospectively at multiple sites across North America using a custom smartphone/tablet application (the Bridge2AI-Voice App) for adults and reproschema-ui for pediatric participants, and comprise acoustic tasks (voice, speech, breathing and cough recordings), detailed demographics, confounder surveys, validated patient questionnaires and patient-reported outcomes, and clinically validated diagnoses. Participants are recruited across five disease cohort categories - voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and pediatric voice and speech disorders - together with controls. The dataset is published as two distinct PhysioNet resources: an adult release (Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information) and a separate pediatric release (Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset). The public releases contain derived audio features (spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch, articulatory and phonetic-posteriorgram features) and phenotypic tables rather than raw audio waveforms; raw audio is disseminated only under controlled access to protect participant privacy."

value: "Bridge2AI-Voice is an ethically sourced, demographically diverse dataset of voice, speech and respiratory sounds linked to multimodal health information, generated by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program. Participants were recruited at specialty (\"high volume expert\") clinics across five sites in North America on the basis of membership in five predetermined disease cohort categories - voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and pediatric voice and speech disorders - together with control participants without those conditions. Each participant completed a standardized protocol of acoustic tasks (sustained phonation, glides, diadochokinesis, breathing and cough sounds, read passages, free speech and cognitive-linguistic tasks), demographic and confounder surveys, and disease-specific validated questionnaires, delivered through a custom tablet application; diagnoses were validated by a qualified clinician against established gold standards or, for the psychiatric cohort, from the electronic health record or an active prescription. The public release is a feature-only (\"AI-ready\") derivation: raw audio waveforms are withheld and the distributed data comprise spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch contours, articulatory (SPARC/EMA) features, phonetic posteriorgrams, openSMILE/Praat static features and audio-quality metrics in Parquet, alongside phenotype and task tables in TSV with JSON data dictionaries. The adult dataset is distributed through PhysioNet; release v3.1.0, published 2026-05-01, covers 833 participants. Raw audio is distributed separately under controlled access via Synapse."
